references.text: The story of the temptation in the Garden of Eden, where Satan tempts Eve, has parallels to the temptation of Jesus, offering something in exchange for worship or disobedience.
God was tempted by Israel's people in the wilderness through their worship of a cast image, which reflects the theme of worshipping anyone other than God.
The prophecy about Lucifer wanting to set himself above God can be seen as a parallel to Satan's desire to be worshipped.
Luke's version of Jesus' temptation, where Satan offers him the glory of all kingdoms in exchange for worship.
